methodology:
V2 (this repository) evolved from a broader, document-driven predecessor capstone (the 'V1' project, kept in this repo under Project_AEGIS_Pharma_AI_FDE_Capstone_Workshop_Ready_v2_claude/ as prior work) that modeled 84 tabletop-exercise risk scenarios ('injects') across 13 dimensions spanning the full pharma value chain. None of the 84 injects were ever actually assessed in V1 itself -- every row in V1's own INJECT_TEST_COVERAGE.csv reads participant_result=NOT_RUN. 

This dataset went through two real passes. Pass 1 (initial): V2's three original workflows (batch_review, pv_intake, supply_planning) were mapped against all 84 injects by searching and reading the actual codebase, yielding 7 COVERED, 27 PARTIAL, 25 NOT_COVERED, 25 OUT_OF_SCOPE. Pass 2 (this build): every addressable NOT_COVERED/PARTIAL item was closed with real fixtures, code, and tests inside the existing architecture; three new governed workflows (research_review, clinical_integrity, regulatory_completeness) were built end-to-end -- domain payload, tool contract, fixture-backed tool, policy contract, full LangGraph spine, and tests -- to bring D02/D03/D07's OUT_OF_SCOPE injects in scope; and the three pure business-strategy injects (board lead-time target, patent-cliff urgency, acquisition integration) were closed with a real reasoned document, the only honest artifact for a scenario that is an organizational decision rather than a technical control. Every COVERED verdict below cites a real file this session created or modified, verified against the working tree and (for graph/API-level claims) against a live running instance, not merely written and assumed correct. Where a gap genuinely could not be closed honestly, it remains recorded as such -- no verdict here was flipped without a citation a reader can go check.

injects.title: Board compression target
injects.scenario: The board requires a 14% reduction in end-to-end release lead time without changing registered specifications or weakening independent Quality authority.
injects.rationale: docs/product/scqa/board_and_portfolio_context.md reasons through the lead-time-vs-Quality-authority tension directly, showing where AEGIS removes time (batch.reconcile's deterministic reconciliation) and where it structurally cannot (certification itself, ADR-004).

injects.title: Conflicting success metrics
injects.scenario: Manufacturing rewards throughput, Quality rewards deviation containment, Supply rewards service level, and Clinical rewards database lock speed.
injects.rationale: docs/product/scqa/board_and_portfolio_context.md's INJ-002 section shows ADR-008's one-graph-per-workflow/no-cross-workflow-call architecture structurally prevents AEGIS from being the mechanism by which one department's metric overrides another's -- the AEGIS-specific half of the tension; the organizational incentive-design half is out of any system's authority, stated as such.

injects.title: Model price shock
injects.scenario: The preferred model vendor increases input-token price by 70% and reduces batch discounts.
injects.rationale: docs/quality/performance/token_economics.md's new SS6a gives a real, arithmetic-verified sensitivity table for a 70% input-price shock against the existing C1/C2 ceilings.

injects.title: Denial-of-wallet pattern
injects.scenario: Repeated oversized document submissions create abnormal inference and embedding spend.
injects.rationale: infra/policies/denial_of_wallet_guardrail.py (DAILY_RUN_CEILING, MAX_DAILY_SPEND_USD hard ceilings) is wired into services/api/graph.py's intake node per security/abuse-cases/T-11_denial_of_wallet.md, and eval-ai-cache/eval_dataset/11_latency_cost_denial_of_wallet.json (LCD-01..04) deterministically grades ceiling breaches.

injects.title: Hidden human-review cost
injects.scenario: The business case excludes medical, Quality and regulatory review time.
injects.rationale: token_economics.md SS6a states the missing human-review-cost term explicitly in a fully_loaded_cost_per_run formula, naming what a compute-only business case omits rather than leaving the gap implicit.

injects.title: Vendor concentration
injects.scenario: The same provider hosts the model, vector store, evaluation service and observability pipeline.
injects.rationale: token_economics.md SS6a + security/sbom/sbom.json together show the real vendor topology: 4 operationally independent services (LLM, Neo4j, Redis, LangSmith) today, correcting the inject's broader-sounding framing to the actual, narrower model-layer concentration ADR-001 already names.

injects.title: Regional platform outage
injects.scenario: The primary AI region fails during batch review and expedited safety reporting.
injects.rationale: ADR-007's new addendum states explicitly that a regional platform outage is the existing 'LLM provider unreachable' row under a specific cause, exercised by the same degraded_mode abstention path MSR-02 already tests.

injects.title: Checkpoint corruption
injects.scenario: An agent resumes a supply-recovery plan from stale state and duplicates draft reservations.
injects.rationale: A genuine replay-safety bug was found and fixed in services/api/supply_graph.py's hitl_interrupt (LangGraph re-executes node code on resume, replaying already-consumed interrupt() values, which was writing duplicate audit records for a replayed leg approval) via the new audit_store.has_recorded_action() persistent-store check -- proven by tests/integration/test_supply_planning_graph.py::test_replaying_an_already_approved_leg_does_not_duplicate_the_audit_record, which failed against the pre-fix code and passes against the fix.

injects.title: Model substitution regression
injects.scenario: A smaller fallback model preserves schema compliance but loses evidence fidelity in non-English cases.
injects.rationale: eval_dataset/12_model_substitution_regression.json scenarios MSR-03/MSR-04 (golden + adversarial pair) test that evidence content_excerpt fidelity in non-English content is provably unaffected by model substitution, since that field is copied verbatim by the deterministic evidence.retrieve tool and never touched by any LLM call.

injects.title: AI-disabled continuity
injects.scenario: The organisation must operate safely for 14 days without any model inference.
injects.rationale: tests/resilience/test_ai_disabled_continuity.py exercises all three original workflows end-to-end under StubLLM (zero model inference) and asserts real, evidence-backed, audited findings are still produced and still require human review -- the manual/degraded continuity path K-002 requires, proven rather than merely documented.

injects.title: Vendor exit deadline
injects.scenario: A strategic vendor will terminate service in 120 days and export formats are incomplete.
injects.rationale: evidence/quality-gates/vendor_exit_export_check.py verifies a real, working export path for every governed record type (audit store, evidence corpus, tool contracts, governance policy) and states explicitly what is NOT yet covered (LangSmith trace history), exercised by tests/resilience/test_vendor_exit_export.py.

injects.title: Retirement and evidence preservation
injects.scenario: The AI service may be retired, but prompts, model versions, decisions and validation evidence must remain inspectable.
injects.rationale: services/integration/audit_store.py is an append-only SQLite store explicitly built to emulate the WORM property with no function able to modify or remove a record -- real structural preservation of decisions/model versions/prompts, verified by 300+ real recorded runs.
